conventions.convention: The root inner product is linear in its first argument. Projective chord distance minimizes Euclidean distance over unit scalar phases between unit representatives.
Projective space has the quotient topology; patch j consists of rays with nonzero jth coordinate, and its coordinates are z_i/z_j in increasing original index order.

Inputs are explicit normalized classical amplitude tables in big-endian basis order. Input length, preprocessing, gates, workspace, depth and error are separate charges; no QRAM or free coherent loading is granted.
A nonzero zero-workspace projection is only a branch. Exact clean output requires the full unconditional output to equal a unit target vector times a unit phase, tensored with zero workspace.

The preparation procedure uses ideal exact arithmetic and explicitly granted continuous-angle gates. Zero-norm prefixes are skipped; leaf phases are relative to the first nonzero amplitude. At n=0 the empty circuit prepares the unique ray.
Isometry completion retains all output coordinates. Extra output wires need not return to zero; width-zero exact circuit synthesis is asserted only for the identity scalar.
Nullity uses countable closed-cube covers. Compact null sets are indexed from zero, and their covers are assigned by least natural codes without a choice principle.

Compilation rephases complete unconditional bounded-arity blocks, including their controls. Its error guarantee concerns the joint output ray and does not assert exact restoration of compiled workspace.

load_bearing.statement: For n≥0, D=2^n, and a normalized explicit amplitude table, alg-qc-state-preparation exactly prepares the target ray using at most D−1 prefix rotations and at most D leaf phases. Its Toffoli flag construction uses O((n+1)D) bounded-arity gates and serial depth and at most max{n−1,0} reusable clean work bits. At n=0 no gate is needed.

Given a valid explicit exact normalized amplitude table, compute prefix norms, apply the specified prefix-controlled rotations with clean Toffoli flags, and apply relative leaf phases; return the continuous-gate circuit and angle table. Invalid length or normalization returns INVALID.
For unit vectors u,v in C^D, d_ch([u],[v])=√(2−2|⟨u,v⟩root|). This is independent of unit representatives and vanishes exactly for equal rays.
For even D≥2 and 0<δ<1/4, there are at least exp(cδD) unit sign vectors with first D/2 coordinates fixed at 1/√D and pairwise projective chord distance at least 2√δ, where cδ=(ln 2/2)(1−H₂(2δ))>0.
For W,A,k≥1 and g≥0, length-g serial descriptions number at most ((k+1)AW^k)^g. A parallel circuit with g occurrences has a serial ordering with the same gate count and denotation.
For m≥1, a sequence (K_i) indexed by i≥0 of compact null subsets of R^m has null union in the closed-cube-cover sense; the proof uses least-coded finite rational-cube covers without choice.
For D≥1 the standard projective patches are smooth charts with coordinate space C^(D−1)=R^(2D−2). For D≥2 each fixed standard patch is proper.
For a prefix p with 0≤|p|<n and r_p>0, θ_p=2 atan2(r_p1,r_p0) satisfies cos(θ_p/2)=r_p0/r_p and sin(θ_p/2)=r_p1/r_p.

seams_checked.note: The fixed-arity compiler is used for complete unconditional blocks with a supplied exact factorization. Whole-block projective error and gate counts are retained; compiler bit-time is explicitly excluded.
Chronological products, ordered local embeddings, occurrence counts and positive gate arity are preserved, including the width-zero scalar exception.
This is contextual: no direct Clifford+T synthesis theorem is invoked. The batch makes no claim of exact arbitrary-angle finite-alphabet implementation or efficient arithmetic synthesis.
QSD is applied directly to WΠ with the stated CNOT bound and width-zero/one exceptions. Fixed-arity factor-count bounds use the unoptimized recursion and the explicit two-qubit base construction.

Controlled rotations are explicitly granted and constructed on ordered control-first supports. Relative phases are retained; projective compiler phases are introduced only after including controls in each complete block.
Targets are pure-state rays represented by normalized nonzero vectors. No vector-level equality is inferred merely from equality of rays.
The stated Y sign and exp(−iθY/2) convention give the displayed real R_y matrix and its positive sine lower-left entry.
Big-endian encoding, tensor-factor order, linear-first pairing, empty register and basis permutations agree with the suppliers.
The Toffoli ladder uses distinct controls and targets, explicitly reverses its computation and reuses restored clean work bits. No arbitrary multicontrol primitive or free oracle is assumed.

The LCU access definition quotes the O((q+1)2^q) continuous-gate bound and max{q−1,0} clean-work count. It permits the preparation phase, explains its cancellation, and separately charges inverse access, table work and finite-gate synthesis.

The optional LCU table construction quotes the correct rotation, phase, gate, workspace and input-bit bounds. Its nonnegative coefficient amplitudes have zero reference argument, so the supplier's ray preparation gives the required vector.

The sorted-XOR sparse-isometry lemma uses the cost model to charge supplied uniform preparation and associated arithmetic/access separately; it does not infer a free preparation circuit or bit-time bound.

The output-and-cost definition accurately identifies the explicit-table continuous-rotation guarantee and keeps input, preprocessing, inverse/control access, finite-gate approximation and classical output costs separate.
